findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Define the RichTextRca contract's field set and any verdict/outcome enum vocabulary (e.g. per-experiment outcome values), mirroring capability-map's explicit-verdict discipline, so the emitted structured finding has a stated shape.
evidence: Plan: 'Returns a structured RichTextRca finding, each experiment cited to evidence ids.'
Plan: 'returns a registered structured RichTextRca contract; it asserts only that a finding was produced'
scripts/jira_dc_capability_map.py:262-363 defines a fully-specified contract with a verdict enum, and _SYSTEM_PROMPT/instructions say verdict must be explicit ('never leave it implicit')
ABSENCE: no field list and no verdict/outcome value vocabulary for RichTextRca anywhere in the plan
findings.finding: The plan names a 'registered structured RichTextRca contract' emitted by the agent but never defines its field set or any verdict/outcome enum vocabulary; the reused sibling contract (JiraDcCapabilityMap) defines every field plus an explicit verdict enum ('present'|'absent'|'present_but_different') and even instructs 'never leave it implicit'.
findings.location: Approach (new files, test module) + AC line 3 ('returns a registered structured RichTextRca contract')
scenarios: An executor must invent the RichTextRca field shape and any outcome/verdict enum, so two implementations produce differently-shaped findings and AC5's 'cited experiment evidence' cannot be checked against a stated shape.
findings.suggested_fix: Sketch the contract in the Approach: RichTextRca(root_cause_hypothesis: str, experiments: list[Experiment], findings: list[str], summary: str) where Experiment carries id, the tool call made, an explicit outcome enum (e.g. 'reproduced'|'not_reproduced'|'inconclusive'), detail, and evidence_ids.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Name the dc_store_copy_repo fixture's isolation (remoteless repos + REBAR_SYNC_PUSH=off) as the load-bearing guardrail that contains run_python's arbitrary-code writes to a throwaway store, and clarify that REBAR_MCP_READONLY=1 only withholds the MCP write tools (not in-process `rebar.edit_ticket`/transport calls) — so the guardrail story is complete for this agent's larger tool surface.
evidence: Plan: run_python is "a persistent in-process REPL warm-started with the transport, compute_update_fields, WikiTextCodec, cutover_clients, dc.run_bridge, rebar"
Plan AC: workflow "sets REBAR_MCP_READONLY=1" as a guardrail, "same guardrails as capability-map"
scripts/jira_dc_capability_map.py: the capability-map agent's ONLY mutation tool is jira_request (raw REST); it has no code-exec tool, so REBAR_MCP_READONLY + throwaway instance fully contains it
src/rebar/_mcp_writes.py:3 — REBAR_MCP_READONLY gates register_write_tools (the MCP write tools), not in-process library calls
tests/external/live_jira_dc/_dc_fixtures.py: dc_store_copy_repo gives 'NEITHER repo gets a remote' and sets REBAR_SYNC_PUSH=off — the actual write-containment layer
findings.finding: The plan claims "same guardrails as capability-map" and relies on REBAR_MCP_READONLY=1, but the run_python(code) REPL executes arbitrary Python in-process (warm-started with `rebar`, the transport, and dc.run_bridge) — a mutation surface REBAR_MCP_READONLY does not constrain. The readonly gate only withholds the MCP write tools (comment_ticket etc.); it cannot stop `import rebar; rebar.edit_ticket(...)` or a direct transport PUT. The real containment for rebar's own ticket store is the dc_store_copy_repo fixture's isolation (remoteless repos + REBAR_SYNC_PUSH=off), which the plan should name as the load-bearing guardrail for the run_python surface rather than importing capability-map's readonly-gate framing that was sufficient there only because that agent has no code-exec tool.
findings.location: Approach / Acceptance criteria ("same guardrails as capability-map"; "sets REBAR_MCP_READONLY=1")
scenarios: The agent, mid-investigation, runs `import rebar; rebar.edit_ticket(...)` or a direct transport mutation via run_python — REBAR_MCP_READONLY=1 does nothing to stop it; only the fixture's remoteless/no-push store keeps it off the real tickets branch

A reviewer or future maintainer reads the AC's REBAR_MCP_READONLY=1 as the write-safety guarantee for the run_python surface and loosens the fixture isolation, silently removing the only real containment

Plan: 'each experiment cited to evidence ids'; AC5: 'uploads a RichTextRca finding with cited experiment evidence'

scripts/jira_dc_capability_map.py:234-245 assigns 'req-NNNN' via len(_EVIDENCE) inside the single jira tool closure; ABSENCE: the plan states no equivalent scheme, and does not say whether run_python outputs are recorded as citable evidence at all
findings.finding: The plan requires each experiment to be 'cited to evidence ids' and AC5 requires 'cited experiment evidence', but never defines how an evidence id is minted or which tool owns the counter — with TWO evidence-producing tools (a persistent run_python REPL and jira_rest) it is ambiguous whether both feed one shared evidence log/counter and how a run_python experiment (arbitrary REPL output) yields a citable id. The reused sibling minted req-NNNN in its single jira tool closure into one module-level _EVIDENCE list, an arrangement the two-tool design does not carry over.
findings.location: Approach (run_python + jira_rest tools) + AC line 3 / AC line 5 ('cited experiment evidence')
scenarios: An executor cannot tell whether run_python calls produce evidence ids, whether the two tools share one counter, or how a REPL experiment is captured for citation — so AC5's 'cited experiment evidence' is unverifiable and the two tools may mint colliding or non-comparable ids.
findings.suggested_fix: Record every run_python and jira_rest call into one module-level evidence list with a monotonic id (e.g. exp-NNNN / req-NNNN) minted in each tool closure before returning, and cite those ids in the contract's evidence_ids fields — mirroring capability-map's _EVIDENCE pattern extended to both tools.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the run_python failure fallback — a raising REPL call returns its traceback/exception text to the agent as the tool result (recorded as evidence), never aborting the agentic run — so a single failed experiment does not prevent a finding being produced.

Plan: 'it asserts only that a finding was produced (an investigation, not a correctness assertion)'

scripts/jira_dc_capability_map.py:171-181/233 — _raw_request catches URLError/TimeoutError/OSError and returns them so the tool always yields an evidence string rather than raising; ABSENCE: the plan states no analogous exception handling for the run_python REPL
findings.finding: The plan specifies the top-level 'investigation, not correctness assertion' posture but no fallback for a failed sub-step of the run_python REPL tool: it does not say whether a run_python call that raises returns the traceback to the agent as a tool result (as the sibling's jira_request returns transport errors as evidence) or aborts the run.
findings.location: Approach (run_python tool) + AC line 3 ('asserts only that a finding was produced ... must not fail merely because the bug still reproduces')
scenarios: The agent runs code that raises (e.g. a transport error or a bad experiment); if the exception propagates out of the tool the whole agentic run can abort and produce no finding, defeating the 'must not fail merely because the bug reproduces' posture.
findings.suggested_fix: In the run_python tool, wrap execution so uncaught exceptions are captured and returned as a string (with an evidence id) rather than propagating, mirroring _raw_request's error-to-string handling.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Justify run_python as a general REPL versus a small set of named diagnostic tools (mirroring capability-map's single narrow jira_request), tying the chosen surface to the current root-cause done-definition rather than to hypothetical future probes.
evidence: grep for 'run_python' returns no matches anywhere in the repo — this is a genuinely new abstraction, not a reuse.
The precedent it cites, scripts/jira_dc_capability_map.py:214-251, gives the agent exactly ONE narrow tool (jira_request: raw REST), not an arbitrary in-process Python REPL over rebar internals.
The plan warm-starts the REPL with transport, compute_update_fields, WikiTextCodec, cutover_clients, dc.run_bridge, rebar — a broad execution surface justified only by one defect investigation.
findings.finding: The run_python persistent-REPL tool is a net-new, broad capability with no existing call-site, exceeding the narrow single-tool precedent the plan claims to reuse.
scenarios: An arbitrary-code REPL over rebar internals is more capability than a single-defect root-cause needs, and is harder to bound than named diagnostic tools.
